questions.q: Why are the environment and costcenter tags applied in the very first az group create command, rather than added later?
options: So every resource created inside the group is tagged from the start, which is exactly what a later cost investigation needs to search on
Tags are required by az vm create and the deployment fails without them
Tags only take effect if they are set before the resource group has any resources in it
Tags are purely cosmetic and have no bearing on later troubleshooting
questions.explain: Tagging the resource group immediately means costcenter and owner are in place before anything else is created — which is exactly what Lesson 31's cost investigation relies on.

questions.q: Why does the VNet get split into web-subnet (10.20.1.0/24) and app-subnet (10.20.2.0/24) instead of putting both VMs in one subnet?
options: So each tier can later carry its own, different security rules — internet-facing for the web tier, restricted for the app tier
Azure requires every VM to be in its own dedicated subnet
A single subnet cannot hold more than one virtual machine
Subnets have no effect on security and are only used for IP address accounting
questions.explain: The whole point of splitting the VNet into two subnets is to give each tier its own security boundary, which Lesson 30's NSG rules then make explicit.

questions.q: What does passing --public-ip-address "" to az vm create for app-vm1 actually accomplish?
options: The app VM is created with no internet-reachable address, so it can't be reached directly from the internet at all
It assigns a randomly generated public IP instead of a named one
It disables the VM's network interface entirely
It has no effect — Azure always assigns a public IP by default
questions.explain: An empty --public-ip-address means the VM gets no public IP resource at all — it can only be reached from inside the VNet, which is the intended design for an app tier.

questions.q: Why is Standard_B2s a reasonable size choice for both web-vm1 and app-vm1 in this lab?
options: It's a burstable, inexpensive size that's appropriate for a small front end and app tier that aren't under constant heavy load
It's the only VM size that supports being placed in a subnet without a public IP
Standard_B2s is required for any VM that will later have an NSG attached to its subnet
Larger VM sizes cannot be created through the Azure CLI
questions.explain: Standard_B2s is a burstable, low-cost size well suited to a small workload — and deliberately not the kind of oversized VM that becomes a cost problem later in this chapter.

questions.q: Why is a separate storage account created for application data instead of just writing files to the VMs' local disks?
options: Application data that needs to persist and be shared shouldn't live only on a VM's local OS/data disk; a storage account is the durable, independent place for it
Azure VMs are not permitted to write any files to their own local disks
Storage accounts are required before any VM can be created in the same resource group
It makes the deployment run faster because storage accounts provision before VMs
questions.explain: A storage account gives the application a durable, independently managed place for uploaded files and logs, separate from either VM's own disk.
